author: Michael Collins

sourceWorks.title: Bardo Thödol (The Tibetan Book of the Dead)
sourceWorks.edition: Undated Holybooks electronic edition; English translation credited to Lāma Kazi Dawa-Samdup, in the Evans-Wentz translation tradition
sourceWorks.provenance: Source supplied by the maintainer: https://dn760101.eu.archive.org/0/items/soi-book-collection-4/The-Tibetan-Book-of-the-Dead.pdf . The 59-page PDF credits the English translation to Lāma Kazi Dawa-Samdup and carries Holybooks.com download notices. Its foreword describes the traditional attribution to Padmasambhava, the revelation by Karma Lingpa, and the first Oxford publication edited by W. Y. Evans-Wentz in 1927. This electronic file does not establish a particular print edition or its own publication date. The repository README independently identifies the Evans-Wentz translation as its basis. These source details are provenance, not a determination of publication rights.

summary: A contemporary devotional rendering of the Bardo Thödol, with forty-five chapters pairing retellings, explanations, and reflections. Tibetan Buddhist imagery of the Clear Light, peaceful and wrathful deities, death, and rebirth opens a contemplation of recognition, compassion, and letting go.
description: Michael Collins brings the Bardo Thödol into a modern devotional voice, following its passages through the Clear Light, peaceful and wrathful visions, and the state of becoming. Each chapter combines a retelling with an explanation and a reflective practice, followed by invocations, prayers, root verses, and a closing blessing. The work explores fear, impermanence, compassion, and awakening in both life and death. It is a creative spiritual adaptation rather than a scholarly translation or a claim to represent every Tibetan Buddhist interpretation; the original source, English translation, and contemporary devotional voice remain distinct.
